text:
tara: Quick heads-up: brought up tiny-ranker-v2 (int8) on staging. Aggregate ndcg@10 +0.018, mrr@1 -0.035. filing here for triage.

ben: interesting. ndcg up but top1 hit takes a hit. classic noise around tie resolution or small scoring shifts.

arjun: did you run on same candidate sets and same seed? even nondet exec order can flip top1.

tara: yes same candidate export, seed=1234. run config: `model=tiny-ranker-v2-int8, batch=128, kvpack=true`. Used our new fast-int8 kernels.

ops-bot: "notice: staging-runner: quant-runtime shows unset deterministic flag"

ben: that flag is a common culprit. set `deterministic=true` and repro. also do fp32 run on the identical query ids for direct per-query diffs.

tara: will do. also planning tokenizer parity check — but pipeline checksums matched for 90% of docs in a quick diff.

naya: another angle: int8 often compresses score variance, increasing tie frequency. Can you dump score CDFs and count exact-equality ties at rank1?

tara: adding histogram dump. quick script: `np.histogram(scores, bins=200)` and `sum(1 for i in ranks if scores[i]==scores[i+1])`

ryan: please also stratify by query length and candidate length; we've seen short queries have more tie issues.

tara: rerun notes: 1) set deterministic=true, 2) fp32 vs int8 per-query top5, 3) score histograms, 4) stratified tie counts. ETA 1.5h.

arjun: for immediate mitigation, try tiny rescale of logits (e.g., multiply scores by 1.01) which can break ties without changing rank order elsewhere. But validate on goldset.

ops-bot: "task created: RANK-847 ensure quant determinism on staging"

(1h later)

tara: quick results: after determinism flag, mrr gap reduced to -0.012 on our 10k prod-sample; ndcg +0.015 persists. tie_count@1 decreased by ~30% but still higher than fp32. per-query diffs show ~120 queries where top1 swapped.

ben: can you paste 3 representative diffs? short queries or queries containing punctuation?

tara: pasted examples inline:
- query: "billing portal"
  fp32 top1: doc_112 (user-friendly billing page)
  int8 top1: doc_998 (billing: legacy page, same content truncated)
- query: "setup webhook"
  fp32 top1: doc_45 (clear steps)
  int8 top1: doc_46 (duplicate snippet in repo)
- query: "oauth callback"
  fp32 top1: doc_77 (official doc)
  int8 top1: doc_77 (same) but score delta tiny (1e-7)

naya: duplicates and truncated html artifacts point to candidate normalization differences. Even if checksums matched for 90%, that 10% can explain MRR. Confirm export time and parser versions.

ryan: also run a bootstrap CI on MRR: 1000 resamples of 2k queries to see if drop is statistically significant.

tara: bootstrap ran: MRR fp32 mean 0.412 ± 0.003, int8 mean 0.409 ± 0.003. Overlap but tails show small shift.

ben: so not catastrophic but noticeable. Two remediation tracks: A) quick mitigation: small rescale (1.02) + deploy to canary; B) long fix: ensure candidate pipeline parity and revisit quant kernels to reduce score compression.

arjun: on the kernel side, raise the quant precision for final FFN output (mixed-int8/float) as an experiment. Could reduce compression while keeping perf.

tara: I'll run A and one kernel tweak B in parallel and post A/B results. artifacts uploaded: https://s3.company/rerank-triage/6887654321 (configs, per-query diffs, histograms).

ops-bot: "scheduled: canary rollout test for rescale multiplier 1.02 on 5% traffic"

ben: final ask — add a small end-to-end checksum test in the onboarding checklist so candidate pipeline drift is detected before model bring-up.

naya: agreed. adding a line item: "candidate-text-checksum parity (utf8 normalized, html-stripped)".

ryan: thanks team. ping here when canary metrics are in. if rescale fixes top1 loss we can keep while kernel patch is validated. :thumbsup:
